# NaNPayloadProbe on GitHub's two runner architectures, 6 November 2026 (VARKA-576), JDK 25.0.5 (Zulu).
# GitHub Actions run 42193042419 on the MaxGekk/spark fork, branch varka-576b-probe-run, which is
# dev/varka_canary/NaNPayloadProbe.java with the canary workflow's default pointed at it. The two
# jobs: ubuntu-latest, an AMD EPYC 9V45 (512-bit species), and ubuntu-24.04-arm, an Arm Neoverse N2
# (CPU part 0xd49, 128-bit species).
#
# Each line is one ordered pair of operands, a quiet or signalling NaN beside another or beside a
# number (105 for each operator and width), the result bits of a scalar Java operation cold and
# after C2 (before and after the slash), and of the Vector API's lanes cold and after C2. DIFF
# marks a line where the four answers differ.
#
# Reading, from the operand pairs with a NaN (105 for each operator and width):
#
# x86 (EPYC 9V45): a scalar subtract, multiply and divide returns the first operand's payload,
#   quieted, in all 105 pairs, at both widths. A scalar add does not follow that rule (65 of 105): a
#   tier may swap an add's operands. The lanes of subtract and divide agree with the scalar answer
#   in every pair; the lanes of multiply (float 40 pairs, double 40) and of add (double 16) differ
#   from it, in pairs of two NaNs only.
# Arm (Neoverse N2): every scalar operation, at both widths, follows Arm's rule in all 105 pairs: a
#   signalling NaN operand's payload quieted, the first such operand when both are, else the first
#   quiet NaN operand's. The lanes agree with the scalar answer in every pair at FLOAT and for
#   subtract and divide at DOUBLE; the lanes of a DOUBLE add and multiply differ from it in 18 pairs
#   each, all of two NaNs, where the lane returns the other operand's payload.
# So the two architectures differ in the payload a subtract or a divide of two NaNs returns (x86
# the first operand's; Arm a signalling operand's first), and in neither can an add or a multiply
# of two unlike NaNs be pinned, which the row rule of VarkaSameAnswer already leaves open.
#
# x86_64, ubuntu-latest (AMD EPYC 9V45)
os.arch amd64  java 25.0.5
float species Species[float, 16, S_512_BIT]  double species Species[double, 8, S_512_BIT]
